extracted.intended_audience: authors submitting papers to arXiv (researchers, scholars preparing preprints)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and requirements for preparing and submitting a paper (text + figures + metadata) to the arXiv preprint archive, including allowed file formats, metadata obligations, timing rules for availability and replacements, and submission responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submitter must be a registered author
rubrics_metrics.description: We accept submissions only from registered authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only users who have registered accounts may submit papers; ensure you register before attempting submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant license to distribute or certify equivalent license
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitters must grant arXiv.org a non-exclusive and irrevocable license to distribute or certify that the work is available under another license that conveys these rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You must either assign the stated license to arXiv or confirm that an alternative license you use grants equivalent distribution rights. This is required to allow public availability on the archive.

rubrics_metrics.name: No omitted figures, tables, sections or abstract-only submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Please note that we do not accept submissions with omitted figures, tables or sections. We also do not accept 'abstract only' submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions missing substantial components (figures/tables/sections) or consisting only of an abstract are unacceptable; they are unhelpful to readers and of very limited archival value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filename character restrictions and case-sensitivity
rubrics_metrics.description: arXiv will only accept the following characters in file names: a-z A-Z 0-9 _ + - . , =. The presence of any other character (e.g. spaces, question marks, asterisks, etc.) will cause the system to reject the entire submission. File names and extensions are also case sensitive on our system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure all submitted filenames use only the allowed characters and correct case; otherwise the system will reject your upload.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the Submit form
rubrics_metrics.description: To submit a paper, use the Submit form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the website's official submit form rather than ad-hoc means; availability and processing follow the archive's procedures described on the site.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted text formats (order of preference)
rubrics_metrics.description: Your submission to the archive must be in one of the following formats (listed in order of preference): (La)TeX, AMS(La)TeX, PDFLaTeX; DOCX (Word 2007); PDF; PostScript; HTML with JPEG/PNG/GIF images.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: arXiv's goal is to store papers in formats which are highly portable and stable; TeX/LaTeX is the best choice because it is an open format that does not hide information. Note that scanned documents are not accepted. Users of older word processors should save as PDF and submit that.

rubrics_metrics.name: No DVI/PS/PDF produced from TeX/LaTeX source accepted
rubrics_metrics.description: For this and other reasons we will not accept dvi, PS, or PDF created from TeX/LaTeX source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you are using TeX/LaTeX, submit source (or PDFLaTeX-produced PDF as allowed) rather than derived DVI/PS/PDF files created from TeX sources; follow arXiv's preferred submission workflows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not submit scanned documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Note also that we will not accept scanned documents, regardless of format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Convert digital source to an accepted format; scans of printed pages are disallowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure file formats allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures for a submission can be in a number of common formats. These include: PostScript (PS/EPS, most common for line drawings, plots, etc.), JPEG (ideal for photographic images), GIF or PNG (best for non-photographic images, bitmaps), PDF figures (only with PDFLaTeX).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose figure formats appropriate to content (EPS/PS for line art, JPEG for photos, PNG/GIF for bitmaps). PDF figures are allowed only when using PDFLaTeX.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep figure file sizes small; do not omit figures even if linked externally
rubrics_metrics.description: If figure files are too large, then readers with poor network connections will not be able to download them. Remember that arXiv has many users with poor network connections (such as users in some developing nations). If your submission has a large figure, be sure to include it, but make all possible efforts to reduce its size. Note that we do not accept submissions with omitted figures, even if you provide a link to another server.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reduce figure resolution/size where possible; include figures in the submission rather than linking externally. See arXiv information on submission sizes and bitmapping help for more information; contact www-admin@arXiv.org if problems arise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use standard TeX macro packages for figures
rubrics_metrics.description: If you submit figures with your (La)TeX source, use standard macro packages (e.g., the graphics and graphicx packages) so that the figures will appear in the document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include figures via standard macros to ensure arXiv's processing renders them correctly. arXiv administration cannot provide TeX-related help, so seek colleague assistance for TeX problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read response and check submission immediately
rubrics_metrics.description: After you submit your paper, you will receive a response from arXiv. It is very important that you read this response. Be sure to check for errors in the copy of the abstract that appears in the message.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check the message for the abstract copy and any generated PostScript; the response includes a URL to view the PostScript version and a username/password for viewing it. If you see errors or formatting problems, act promptly to replace the paper or contact support as directed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replace papers to correct errors; do not make a new submission
rubrics_metrics.description: We encourage authors to update and to make corrections in their papers. DO NOT make a new submission for a corrected paper or for an erratum. Rather replace the original submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the 'replace' mechanism to submit corrections or errata. If you replace before 16:00 US Eastern time (EDT/EST) Monday through Friday, the archive software will not generate an additional date stamp. If you cannot correct problems yourself, email www-admin@arXiv.org explaining the problem before 16:00 US Eastern time; do not send files to that address.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authors must submit their own papers (take responsibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: Because putting papers on the archives entails certain responsibilities, authors must make their own submissions. Third-party submissions (by secretaries for example) are often the ones that cause the most problems, presumably due to lack of self-interest and related factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The submitting author should be the responsible party for the submission process to avoid errors and issues arising from third-party submitters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide required metadata (institutional affiliation and report numbers)
rubrics_metrics.description: The following information is also required for submission: Institutional affiliation for the author(s) must be provided. Official report number(s) from the author(s) institution(s) must be provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete metadata fields accurately; missing required metadata may impede processing or discoverability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission availability schedule and timing rules
rubrics_metrics.description: All archives are on a daily availability schedule, with no activity scheduled on weekends. Each day's submissions are not made available to the general public until 20:00 US Eastern time (EDT/EST) Sunday through Thursday.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand timing: e.g., a submission before 16:00 US Eastern on Monday is available after 20:00 that day and appears in the Tuesday AM mailing; submissions on Friday before 16:00 are available after 20:00 Sunday and appear in Monday AM mailing; submissions after 16:00 Friday are available after 20:00 Monday and appear in Tuesday AM mailing. Plan replacements and submissions around these cutoffs.

rubrics_metrics.name: All official submitted versions are publicly available
rubrics_metrics.description: Note further that all official versions of submitted papers are made publicly available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that versions you submit become public records; consult the discussion of submission version availability for details on visibility of different versions.
